history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration complete further the information disclosed in the notes to the financial statements, as prescribed in paragraphs 141 to 149 of IPSAS 39: Employee benefits.
history.administration_response: The Administration further discussed this topic with Board during the audit of volume II statements for the year ended 30 June 2023 and agreed to supplement the notes to the financial statements by disclosing the maturity profile of annual leave and repatriation benefits liabilities. The Administration disclosed all significant assumptions and included a sensitivity analysis in the notes, ensuring compliance with the disclosure requirements of IPSAS 39.
history.board_assessment: The Administration disclosed the durations/maturities of repatriation grants and accrued annual leave plans. However, the Administration has not disclosed the expected contributions for the 2023/24 financial year in note 16 to the financial statements for the present year, as required by paragraph 149 (b) of IPSAS 39. Those contributions shall be determined on the basis of expected benefit payments for 2023/24. Their disclosure is not conditional on the existence of a funding mechanism. The Board considers the recommendation to be under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: In paragraph 293 of its report, the Board recommended that the Administration complete further the information disclosed in the notes to the financial statements, as prescribed in paragraphs 141 to 149 of IPSAS 39: Employee benefits.

history.sg_progress: The Administration will hold a discussion with the Board on this recommendation during the interim audit of 2024 and request its subsequent closure. The Administration believes that, as confirmed by the independent actuary, paragraph 149 (b) of IPSAS 39 is applicable to reporting entities that have funded liabilities (i.e. the amount the entity expects to pay to the plan in the next reporting period). In addition, it should be noted that paragraph 149 (b) appears in IPSAS 39 under the heading “Amount, timing and uncertainty of future cash flows”, meaning its goal is to inform users of the financial statements of the future cash flows associated with the defined benefit plan. Since after-service health insurance is funded only after claims are made, the United Nations cannot anticipate contributing a specific amount in the next reporting period. The amounts paid for medical claims will only be known when they are presented for payment (pay as you go), which is not certain at the time the financial statements are issued. The Administration could use the actuarial model to project the future year’s cost; however, this amount would not translate to cash outflow for the United Nations. Therefore, the Administration believes that including the amount of expected benefit payments in the notes is not relevant in the Organization’s case and might mislead the users of the financial statements. With regard to disclosing maturity/duration periods for repatriation grants and annual leave, the Administration has complied with this requirement in the financial statements for the financial period ended 30 June 2023.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration complete further the information disclosed in the notes to the financial statements, as prescribed in paragraphs 141 to 149 of IPSAS 39: Employee benefits.
history.administration_response: The Administration will hold discussion with the Board on this recommendation during the interim audit of 2024 and request subsequent closure. The Administration believes that, as confirmed by the independent actuary, paragraph 149 (b) of IPSAS 39 is applicable to reporting entities that have funded liabilities (i.e., it is the amount that the entity expects to pay to the plan in the next reporting period). In addition, it should be noted that paragraph 149 (b) appears in IPSAS 39 under the heading “Amount, timing and uncertainty of future cash flows” (i.e., the goal of IPSAS 39 is to inform users of the financial statements of the future cash flows associated with the defined benefit plan). Given that after-service health insurance is not funded, the United Nations does not anticipate contributing a specific amount in the next reporting period. The amounts paid for medical claims will be known only when they are presented for payment (pay as you go), which is not certain at the time financial statements are being issued. While the Administration could use the actuarial model to project the future year’s cost, this amount would not translate to cash outflows for the United Nations. Therefore, the Administration believes that including the amount of expected benefit payments in the notes is not relevant in the case of the United Nations and might mislead the readers of the financial statements. With regard to disclosing maturity/duration periods for repatriation grant and annual leave, the Administration complied with this requirement in the 30 June 2023 financial statements.
history.board_assessment: Considering the comments and details given by the Administration in October 2024, the Board agrees to close the recommendation.
